body:
When I just ran `devvm start`, I got:

> error: Failed to start domain 'empty-main'
> error: Requested operation is not valid: network 'default' is not active

Maybe devvm should start that network, too (or ask to start it, if auto-starting is considered rude)
title: devvm should start the vm's network if it isn't already running

body:
Some notes from first use:

- For `DEVVM_POOL_DIR` an existing libvirt pool was accepted (I prefer to manage these myself), but then the actual permissions aren't checked (it tries to make a directory in there called `base`, which fails if that directory isn't owned by me). 
- I liked the guidance after `./install.sh` - next step is clear. `devvm setup` should have the same!
- I don't understand the claudism in the "linked worktree" paragraph in the readme 🤷 what is "at that path"?
- `devvm create` hangs before "cloud-init done"  if I do the `devvm ssh sudo tail [..]`  thing in another terminal (my guess: `create` waits for its `ssh` connection to finish, which it doesn't, because in my setup, the first `ssh` command makes the connection which is re-used by subsequent `ssh` calls to that same host; `devvm ssh` should disable ssh control master and just make a new connection every time)
- `devvm create` again has good next steps
- `devvm setup-dev` should maybe separate out some things; I don't always need claude, but git identity is almost always useful. Could be interactive?
title: First use notes
